transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's, uh, it's real nice to meet you too. Thank you for seeing me. 

I, um... well, I hope I'm explaining this right. I came in because... I just feel like I've got this, like, a motor running inside me all day? It's probably nothing too bad, but... if I have to sit still for very long, like at church, or out there in the waiting room, or even just sitting at home, I get this... this trapped feeling. Like I just absolutely have to get up or do something. I try real hard not to be a bother to anybody, I promise, but it just gets so uncomfortable. Does that... does that make sense to you, Doc? Is that okay to come in for?
Have you felt this way for most of your life, even when you were a child, or is this something that started more recently?

Well, um... yes, sir. I guess it's been pretty much my whole life. Even back when I was just a little boy. 

I don't want you to think I was a bad kid or anything, I really did try to behave, I promise. But, um... back in school, the teachers were always having to move my seat around. I just... I couldn't seem to stay put, no matter how hard I tried. And sometimes I'd accidentally talk out of turn, or I'd get in a little bit of trouble for jumping up out of my chair before class was even done. I always felt real bad about it, making extra work for them and all. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about, Dr. Smith? I hope I'm giving you the right answers.
Aside from the trouble staying still or waiting your turn, do you find that you have a hard time keeping your attention on tasks or staying organized?

Well, um... I really do try my best to pay attention, I promise I do. I don't want you to think I'm ignoring folks on purpose or being rude. But... yeah, sometimes it's a little tricky for me. 

Like, if folks are talking through the times we're supposed to get rides, or going over the pantry lists, or even just the plans for church... I listen real good right at the start. I'm right there with them. But then... I don't know, my mind just sort of slips off somewhere else. And then I realize I missed some pieces that I really needed to hear. 

I always feel awful when I have to ask them to repeat it. I try so hard to keep it all straight in my head. Does that... does that sound like what you were wondering about, sir? I hope I'm explaining it okay.

When you look at your day-to-day life right now as an adult, do you feel that your struggles with staying focused and organized are just as significant as your struggles with feeling restless and needing to move?

Well, um... I guess... I guess they both give me a bit of trouble, yes, sir. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know I just need to try harder to keep things straight. 

But, um, with the organizing part... I try to keep all my things neat, I really do. It's just that my papers, and the little appointment cards they give me, and the food boxes, and even the notes I try to put in my phone... they just sort of get all mixed up together somehow. I look at it all, and I just can't quite figure out what needs doing first. And then, before I know it, things are already late or I've messed something up. 

I always feel so bad when it happens, like I'm letting people down. I'm really trying my best to keep it all organized. Is that... is that the kind of thing you meant, Dr. Smith? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I just want to make sure I'm answering you right.
